questions.question: Given `enum Status { Active, Inactive }`, what does `Status[1]` evaluate to at runtime?
options: A compile error, because enums cannot be indexed
questions.explanation: Numeric enums compile to an object with a reverse mapping from number to name, so Status[1] is "Inactive". String enums do not get a reverse mapping.

questions.question: What is the type of `pincodes.Pune` in `const pincodes = { Mumbai: 400001, Pune: "411001" } satisfies Record<string, number | string>;`?
questions.explanation: satisfies checks compatibility with the target type but keeps the value's own inferred type, so Pune stays string. An annotation would have widened it to number | string.

questions.question: Why does running a file containing `enum Role { Admin = "ADMIN" }` directly with Node's built-in type stripping fail?
options: Enums generate runtime JavaScript, so they are not erasable syntax and strip-only mode rejects them
Node requires a tsconfig.json to run any .ts file
String values are not allowed in .ts files run by Node
questions.explanation: Type stripping can only delete type annotations. Enums, namespaces and parameter properties need code generation, so Node throws ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX in strip-only mode.

questions.question: `const METHODS = ["UPI", "CARD"] as const;` — what is `(typeof METHODS)[number]`?
questions.explanation: as const infers a readonly tuple of literal types. Indexing that tuple type with number gives the union of its element types: "UPI" | "CARD".
